chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from al-Ash'ari, from Samakah ibn Mihran, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Verily, Allah, the Exalted, did not send any Prophet or Imam except that he is the most knowledgeable of the people regarding Allah's affairs.'

He said: 'And He does not command them except with what Allah commands them, nor does He forbid them except with what Allah forbids them, nor do they assume any matter of Allah's affairs except by His command.'
He said: 'If they were more knowledgeable of Allah's affairs than the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) or the commander of the person...'
He said: 'Then they would not be the allies of Allah.'

key_terms.أَعْلَمُ النَّاسِ: The most knowledgeable of the people
key_terms.إِمَام: Imam (leader/successor, often with connotation of infallibility in Shia theology)

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between the knowledge of the Prophet/Imam and the command of Allah?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq utilizes this hadith to substantiate the doctrine of *Ismah* (infallibility), arguing that the Prophet and Imams possess complete knowledge of divine affairs to serve as perfect guides. It highlights their role as *Awliya’ Allah* (God’s allies) whose commands are not autonomous but directly derived from Allah, ensuring their teachings are free from error and independent action.
